title: Devlog #1: building a 1400s Venetian trading game with Claude Code.
author: Harvan29
selftext:
Hi everyone :)

This is my first devlog, and I'm going to try to post one every Monday. I'm Harvan, a solo dev from Italy, and I'm making **Fondaco – A Venetian Merchant's Tale**, a historical trading strategy game set in the Mediterranean of 1400 (Unity 6, PC, single-player). It has 47 cities rebuilt from historical plans, 19 goods, 18 AI trading companies and a map made from real geographic data. **Almost all of it is built with Claude Code.**

There's no demo yet and the Steam page is on its way. For now there's the Discord: [https://discord.gg/pfvD334RUK](https://discord.gg/pfvD334RUK) and the site: [https://www.fondacogame.com](https://www.fondacogame.com/)

**What got done this week**:

**Pirates now give you options**. When a corsair catches you, you pick: Fight, Pay the toll, Surrender the cargo, or Auto-resolve. When you're the one attacking: Attack, Demand surrender, Auto-resolve, or Leave it. Ships give up based on morale (a merchant ship folds fast, a corsair almost never), they furl their sails and "Surrenders" shows up above them. The end of a battle used to be a big sign; now it's a short report with the outcome and the numbers.

**Warehouses aren't free anymore.** A \*fondaco\* is a merchant's warehouse in a foreign city (that's where the name of the game comes from). You start with one, in your home city. Anywhere else it costs 4,000 ducats if you have a guarantee (your own nation, a permit or a letter of recommendation) and 20,000 if you don't. You get a letter through reputation: once you reach 50% in a nearby city, you can ask its guild for one. The guild shows your progress ("Genoa 34% of 50%"), and all 47 cities have a guild now. Owning a fondaco cuts that city's duty by 25%, lets you enter the city without a ship in port, and caravans only run between your own fondaci.

**Walls around 45 cities.** That's every city except Venice (my call) and Milan, which already had its own. It's one Lombard wall kit recoloured by culture and placed procedurally: towers climb the slopes, battlements follow the ground, gate towers sit a few metres off the gates. No new 3D models for this. The forest used to grow straight through the walls and fill a whole quarter of the city with trees; now it starts outside.

**Milan got its monuments**: the Duomo, the Castello Sforzesco, the Palazzo della Ragione and the Loggia degli Osii. Confession for the history people: in 1400 the Duomo was a building site, and the Castello you know is the Sforza rebuild from the 1450s. I kept the famous versions on purpose, same as Brunelleschi's dome in Florence (finished in 1436). They're written down as anachronisms in the city's plan, so at least they're deliberate 😄

**Bugs and small things:**

* Rival companies' sales were showing up as \*your\* messages and in \*your\* profit and loss. Very generous of them, but no.
* When the sun was low, the sails got a stair-step shadow. I spotted it on a video clip; it's fixed in the sail shader now.
* The invisible plane that keeps the sea out of the hulls was poking out of the sides: a white stripe on 6 of the 21 hulls, and sea water inside the hold of two cogs.
* Citizens had white cracks on their clothes because the cloth mask only covered about 70% of the texture.
* Milan's river kept breaking up into puddles. The fix was one line (terrain pixel error from 4 to 1).

**In the lab (not in the game yet):** boarding, with grappling hooks, a duel, a melee across both decks, weapons by culture, and archers (one fighter in five, max 4 per ship). Also shore defenses at the Lido mouth of the Venetian lagoon: a trebuchet, a catapult, a cannon tower and a lookout that actually shoot at a real ship. The boulder casts a falling shadow that shows where it's going to land.

**Workflow:**

Anything big starts in a lab scene that isn't in the build. Boarding and the shore defenses live there until they're good; the game doesn't touch them yet. That way Claude can rebuild them as many times as it takes without breaking the real game.

A few rules from my CLAUDE.md:

* Venice, Genoa and Ragusa are cities I placed by hand. Claude doesn't move anything in them without asking me.
* Meshy and ElevenLabs cost credits, so it asks before every paid generation. This week that was 53 Meshy credits for the mosque, 166 ElevenLabs credits for two sound clips, and 0 for the walls.
* It only commits when I type the word "commit".
* The game starts on 1 January 1400, no anachronisms. Except the ones I add myself in Milan, apparently.
* When it makes a design choice on its own, it has to tell me before I approve. For the mosque model it removed the shops and went with a flat roof and battlements, and it said so before I said ok.

This week I also added three "production" skills, adapted from claude-code-game-studios: one checks what I ask for against the demo plan and tells me when I'm scope-creeping or running late, one does the economy (prices, routes, how many ducats you make in a year), and one handles playtest notes. They're read-only until I tell them to write.

**What I use**

(People ask what I use for assets, so here's the list:)

1. **Claude Code (Opus 5.5), Ultra plan**: basically all the building. All the code and shaders, the wall generator, the warehouse and reputation systems, the Blender scripts (run headless), the Steam page texts and the new cut of the trailer in Remotion.
2. **Meshy**, Premium plan: the 3D models. This week Milan's four monuments and the mosque for the 12 cities of the Maghreb and Egypt (two reference images, then the 3D model). My pipeline is Meshy → Blender headless (fixes, LODs, sometimes new materials) → Unity, with 3 LODs and 4K textures.
3. **ElevenLabs**, Premium plan: sounds. This week, two 25-second clips for the mosque.
4. **Gemini**, base plan: 2D art. The coats of arms on flags and sails, and the event and panel illustrations.
5. **Mixamo**: part of the animations (i.e archers,...).
6. The map comes from open geodata (Copernicus, GEBCO, ESA WorldCover), processed in **QGIS**.
7. **Unity 6** is the engine.

That's it for this week. Any feedback is appreciated :)

comments.author: FraffoD
comments.body: fantastico ho adorato patrician 3 e avevo in mente di creare qualcosa del genere, ma se realizzi tu un gioco cosi bello ancora meglio

replies.author: Harvan29
replies.body: Thank you. I am working to improve tho 😅

comments.author: milox88
comments.body: molto molto interessante. una domanda: se non ho capito male generi gli asset 3d in meshy e poi li fai implementare a codex dopo un passaggio in blender per la rifinitura, giusto?

replies.author: Harvan29
replies.body: Prima fornisco una descrizione molto dettagliata di quello che vorrei e una serie di immagini reference. Poi Claude code genera un'immagine 2d con meshy tramite MCP server sulla base delle mie info. Se approvo, genera il 3d con meshy. Poi, sempre con Claude code lo faccio passare in blender con codice sistemando i Lod e facendo qualche altro aggiustamento. Se c'è bisogno ritocco qualcosina io in Blender. Infine, Claude Code importa il risultato finale in Unity sempre con MCP.

comments.author: mwisconsin
comments.body: Hilarious. I was in early stages of developing this exact game -- because I miss Rise of Venice. You're just a little further along than me. I'll just follow you and stop spending tokens. :)

comments.author: explocion200
comments.body: Looks cool !!! Saved so i can come back for play test

comments.author: spzzgmnspysgmn
comments.body: Always interesting to see someone try out a niche like a historical trading simulation. There's a few titles in the past but it remains a niche that could use more games in it. The fact that Claude is helping you take this on as a solo project is also pretty intense as a game like this seems like it be the work of a small dev team in the recent past just to be feasible.

replies.author: Harvan29
replies.body: I believe there is so much potential in this game category! From Patrician IV, every game has been a flop. I believe there are many people like me begging for a good historical trading simulation. Let's see in 2027 if i am wrong or not ☺️

comments.author: Many_Translator1720
comments.body: Awesome devlog! Quick FinOps tip if you're generating lots of NPC dialogue lines in ElevenLabs: use Flash v2.5 / Turbo v2.5 for ambient merchant and barks dialogue and save Multilingual v2 strictly for hero cutscenes. Flash bills at 0.5 credits per character (\~500 credits/min instead of \~1,000 credits/min), which immediately doubles how many voice lines you get out of your monthly credit pool.

comments.author: Shadeun
comments.body:
This looks incredibly similar to Merchant Prince//Machiavelli trading game from decades ago (which I loved). I assume its inspired by it heavily?

EDIT: in fact im pretty sure you're even using the same layout and some of the art assets?

replies.author: Harvan29
replies.body: The art is mainly based on real architecture of the period. In some case (i.e. Basilica di San Marco, other monuments,...), it Is based on the exact layout and images of existing buildings.

replies.author: Harvan29
replies.body: H2 2027. However, stay tuned for more updates!
